newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees Santos container terminal sold by Aug.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees Santos container terminal sold by Aug.

text.p: Brazil hopes to privatize the country's biggest container terminal at Santos port by August and speed up the privatization of the port sector as a whole, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.

"As part of a complete reevaluation of the criteria for privatization of ports, we have established a timetable for the sale of the main terminal at Santos," Kandir told reporters after a meeting of National Privatization Council.

Sao Paulo port authority Codesp had been asked to send a proposed minimum price for the terminal within 30 days to the National Development Bank (BNDES) which oversees Brazil's privatization program, the minister said.
The BNDES would then prepare tender details for the sale within a further 15 days and a privatization auction could take place two months later, he said.
"The auction will take place in August at the latest," said Kandir, who has regularly said port privatization is a key step towards boosting Brazil's exports.
BNDES privatization director Jose Pio Borges said the government was in a hurry to speed up port privatization in time for shipments of this year's expected bumper grains harvest.
As well as the container terminal, Codesp recently published tenders for the privatization of seven other areas of Santos port, he said.
